grafts: comedian: the micro wiper clears a frost patch shaped like a question mark that freezes back behind it, at the open, and frost creeps back toward the eye at the button

explainer: the three kinds of work as three lanes (a roadside logger, a specialist at the wheel, a cone course), four traction gauges under the wheels, a glass road poured digitally under a SIMULATION label
enthusiast: one warm weather-station puck pulling back to an abstract snow field of unnumbered pings, ILLUSTRATIVE
treatment.judge_reasoning: The residents' question is about seeing, and the thing that sees is the roof sensor puck, so the hero is the eye of the car with a face and the car stays a dark silhouette. Every mechanism Waymo published (heaters, micro wipers, stated backup sensing, traction under each wheel, simulated ice) is a state change on that one object, which makes the design legible without a single photoreal vehicle. The skeptics get their own roadside billboards at full strength, and the film concedes that every answer so far is on paper. The button leaves the puck half frosted on a vast dark road: the winter is the test.

palette.mood: a bright, milky Fairbanks noon that dims to whiteout and ends in one lamp at night; curious and hopeful, amber only where a machine is working
palette.why: Fog-filtered pink-gold reads as Interior Alaska winter daylight, which is the honest setting of the test and warm enough for a hopeful valence. The paper step and plum ink keep text off the hoarfrost hero so the puck owns the lightest value.
palette.divergence: 11-10 was a true violet blue hour with a vermilion machine and an acid lemon lamp, 11-08 permafrost, 11-07 transformer teal, 11-06 tangerine office, and 11-02 keyed its whole cab in sodium amber. No violet or purple surfaces or light anywhere, plum is ink only. No lemon at all. Amber is emitted light on mechanisms only, never the key, so it does not repeat 11-02. Recorded overlap: 11-09's oxblood courtroom sits in the crimson family; here crimson is one emitted tail light, once, not a surface or a world.

light.light_story: ice-fog noon (act 1), whiteout (shots 5, 6 and 11), one cold LED lamp in the evening (shot 13)

shape_language: PRIMARY axis: the smooth domed puck and its soft round rings, lens and gauges against jagged crystalline rime, fern frost and broken ice. Every state change is round smoothness winning or losing ground to jagged crystal. SECONDARY: the rectilinear road, lanes, billboards, phone and paper. WHY: the story is a machine meeting a winter, so the machine is drawn smooth and the winter is drawn jagged, and a muted viewer can read who is winning from the silhouette of the frost.

casting.hero: RoofPuck (net-new, lib/sensors.tsx), the roof sensor dome with a face: two tiny wiper-arm eyebrows, a frost-rimmed brow, a round lens eye that opens, narrows or goes blind white. Graphite #2A2F36 body, hoarfrost rim. Params frost 0..1, clearRing 0..1, mode 'blind'|'backup'|'wheel'|'clear', emotion, glow. Reusable for any sensor, camera or vehicle-autonomy story.

casting.reasons: The shelf has no sensor or autonomous-vehicle asset. The roof puck is the one gap, built as a reusable library asset. Yesterday's TakeANumberMachine and the recent StampBot, Reels and Strand heroes are not used. dedupe.py check returned FRESH for RoofPuck. Alaska Native subjects: none.

motion_language: The puck breathes on its mount, its wiper eyebrows twitch on effort and its lens iris dilates and narrows with springs, never linear. Frost creeps in as jagged fern growth and melts in smooth rings from the heater outward. Lanes, gauges and billboards enter with anticipation, overshoot and settle. The whole frame jolts only on the three board kicks.

composition.focal_hierarchy: each shot names one 55 to 70 percent hero, a 20 to 30 percent support and 10 to 15 percent world; the puck is off-center in shots 2, 5, 9 and 13
composition.info_placement: plates live where the information lives: on objects (puck, lanes, map pins, clipboard), on the phone screen, on billboards, in the puck's HUD, in side plates left or right, and in the lower third only on a minority of beats
composition.negative_space: the vast dark road around one small car under one lamp at the close, and the half second of silence after the crimson blink
composition.safe_area: hero and plates within y 420 to 1500 of the 9:16 master, fog sky above and road and snowbank below stage the vertical
composition.signature_shot: the cold open: a mittened hand wipes a frosted window, a headlight sweeps a dry-looking road, the road becomes a mirror holding the frosted puck upside down, then one micro wiper clears a question-mark arc and the eye opens on 'Do they know to look for black ice?'
composition.stamp_cap: No rubber stamps. Plates are BoxLabels, billboard quotes, the sheet and the clipboard. Added labels on drawn things are SIMULATION on the glass road, VALIDATED LIMIT on the gauge line, WHAT IF on the thought-frame and ILLUSTRATIVE on the fleet field, the mile markers and the mirror road.
composition.honesty: Nothing says Waymo named Fairbanks: the post plate reads ALASKA and the Fairbanks pin arrives with the governor's card. The whiteout backup is Waymo's stated design (c19), not observed behaviour. The stalled car is the skeptic's worry in a thought-frame, not an event. The fleet field has no geography and no number, and the counter reads blank. No driverless claim and no timeline: the pen never writes. The billboard row has no figures. The thought-frame shoulder and the shot 11 shoulder are the same composition, so the worry and the stated pause are drawn as one place.

craft_advance: the net-new RoofPuck sensor asset with a face, frost and clear-ring states; nothing else this film needs
